During your six months in the HZ HB, did you notice anything indicating that this was in fact the case, that the HVO were doing everything to lend support to all forms of criminal behaviour, or indeed that this was their official policy, to back such behaviour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Counsel, that is not what was said. What was said was that by -- by not prosecuting criminals, that was an effect that was created, but I look up the -- if you think I'm wrong, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was listening and writing down my questions because this is something that stuck with me, so I believed immediately that this is a question that needs to be asked of the general, whether the HVO was implementing a policy that promoted crime. I thought to myself immediately this is a question I need to raise, and right now, I'm unable to track it down; nevertheless, my learned friend Mr. Kovacic can perhaps give me a hand with that. We were discussing P7812, that was the document we were discussing at the time and that's when this occurred. I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAWS
utterances.text: As it's the suggestion that it's my question, I respectfully disagree. I suggested that a policy was adopted which had the result -- produced that result, not that that was the intention of it, that it was low down the list of priorities and it was keeping people at the front line that was priority. That's what I suggested, and I hope that's being clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best to track down the reference in the transcript, but I could perhaps rephrase my question at any rate. I know that's what I heard. That's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: General, in your opinion, while you were down there in the HZ HB monitoring the lines and the HVO and exercising control over there, could you conclude that the HVO deliberately favoured a policy of not punishing perpetrators and of promoting indiscipline among the ranks of their own men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor told everyone what his question was, and the question that you're putting to Mr. Skender is a bit different, because the Prosecutor told us that as far as he was concerned, the HVO's priority was the front line, and all the rest was no priority, was none of his business. That's what I understood anyway. But the question that you're put something is at a different level.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's very difficult to be rummaging through the transcript all the time and remaining in charge of my re-examination. I know it was my mistake, not taking down the page number, but it was a general question and that submission was part of the question. That's why I asked the general the question, but I'm prepared to drop that question anyway. All right. I'll move on. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: General, I'm not showing it to you because you don't have it in front of you, but my learned friend, Ms. Nozica, showed you P01077. This was a document when you talked about the questions whether there was some positions of command to which persons were appointed who were not up to it, who were not sufficiently qualified, to be commanders or assistant commanders. P1077. The only reason I'm invoking that document is to bring up a number of topics that were mentioned during cross-examination. You said that certain situations occurred where certain persons -- persons were appointed to certain positions simply because there was no one else available, or perhaps these people came to be in those positions through some contacts that they had. Well, what I'd like to ask you is based on your experience and your knowledge what do you believe if we have persons who are not sufficiently qualified to work as commanders or assistant commanders or exercise any command function at all? Was the only thing that mattered not for them to have the proper qualifications and education?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SKENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was a kind of war where what was important was to be intelligent. The operations were complex, were complicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: General, do you believe that General Praljak was not a skilled commander and that he was not in charge of leading the HVO simply because he had not received appropriate military training?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR SKENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that he was very competent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, I would like to place an objection. I will not be asking any questions since I do not have the right to do that. I'm talking about document P04177. My learned friend brought it up on redirect, talking about who received Mr. Luka Markesic's report on developments referred to by the Prosecutor during their cross-examination. The document was drafted by the assistant brigade commander Rama for security and information, and the only thing that I'm trying to do, and this must be about the third time that I'm doing it in this courtroom, the last time that happened during -- it was towards the end of the cross of Mr. Praljak, I'm pointing out page 2 and page 3 in the English where we find the following expressly: "Regardless of who received this document, the author of this document claims that the brigade commander, too, had been informed of all these developments." I don't believe this is something my learned friend did on purpose or deliberately, I think it was due to an oversight, but within the larger framework of all the questions that she asked, I would like yet again to draw your attention to that particular detail in this particular document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your comment is now on the transcript, and the Judges will take it into account. General, your testimony is now over. On behalf of my colleagues and myself, I thank you for coming to testify here for the Praljak Defence and helping us -- helping justice. I wish you a safe return home, and I will ask our usher to please escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have just a few minutes left. Mr. Kovacic first. Earlier you answered by -- and told us that you sent a written submission today regarding the question I put to you earlier on the question of the admissibility of documentary evidence. We've looked at your submission, written submission, but you're not answering the question that was put to you. We want to know which topics you will address and when you will address these topics, and there's nothing -- no mention of this in your submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I sent document before you raised the question today. As I said, I have answered some of the points that you raised today. Anything else I can answer tomorrow in an organised manner and calmly and instead of improvising and leaving something unsaid. At any rate, as the document is, which is something that you've seen, we believe we cannot move by place and location, which something that you indicate but in no binding way in guideline number 9 unless I'm wrong, but we can do this in an organised manner tomorrow and tell you what topics we'll be raising. One thing I can certainly say is we shall do our best to simplify the entire matter and make it easier for everyone. Our plan is to write one motion, a consolidated motion, if you like, instead of several motions, which will then have annexes arranged by subject matter. There will be several topics, eight or nine, as I currently believe. Some of these may be further subdivided, but each subject will be defined by particular relevant points what the relevance is of a certain topic, and then there will be a list of documents, too, document sources, relation to the indictment and so on and so forth. If you would like me to, I can brief you on all of this in an organised manner tomorrow. I don't think that should be a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When do you intend to give us this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are certain that we can do this by the 26th of October, which is the date you set as the start of the next Defence case. We very much hope that we can get this done much earlier, but we simply cannot be held to something that we can't really promise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. Thank you for this information. You know that tomorrow we will start at 9.00. We know that the witness is ready. So we'll resume tomorrow. I wish you all a pleasant evening. It's almost 7.00 p.m., unless Ms. Pinter would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One second, please. Page 82, line 25, and page 83, lines 1 through 3. The question was recorded exactly as I put the question to the witness by the Prosecutor previously. It was just for the transcript. I didn't just come up with that question. This is what it says: "Finally, I'm putting it to you that the use of forced labour was ..." on page -- or, rather, "went the same way as the HVO had when they were implementing their policies of not supplying discipline, order, and law and order." Therefore, the question was asked. I didn't just make it up, but it was part of a rather long question. Just for the transcript. Just to make sure that it reflects the fact that my quote was accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAWS
utterances.text: May I reply to that as well. The transcript will show that that's nothing like the question it was suggested I had asked. So I just want to be clear about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is adjourned 'till tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
